subject: Immediate: Reserved-capacity shortfall & GPU farm saturation — exec readout
body:
From: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@aurorabank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike: errors + latency on reserved pool (Aurora production)

Vanessa —

We started seeing a large spike in 5xxs and tail latency around 07:45 PDT. Impacting inference for our fraud model (p95 latency jumped from 120ms to ~1.2s and error rate to ~3.6%). We are on the reserved GPU pool you provisioned (reservation AU-7742). This is causing ~18% of requests to timeout at our gateway and failing order scoring.

We attached a short snapshot of request rates and error samples. Can you confirm whether this is a noisy neighbor issue or a reserved throughput shortfall? We are in a tight weekend window and need immediate mitigation or a burst authorization.

—Lina
Lead SRE, AuroraBank

---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Moreno <lina.moreno@aurorabank.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2027 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: errors + latency on reserved pool (Aurora production)

Hi Lina — thanks for the heads up and the snapshots. We're seeing the same signal in our telemetry. Initial notes:

- Reserved pool AU-7742 experienced a rapid QPS increase starting ~07:40 PDT; backlog on KV cache and token queues increased.
- Some nodes reported higher GPU mem pressure leading to sporadic OOM throttles and 5xx returns.
- Automatic fallback to compatible model variant did not fully engage for a subset of routes due to pinned routing rules.

I'm looping in David (runtime) and Marissa (account lead) to triage. Short term ask: can you keep a window open for an emergency failover/cutover? We may request burst authorization from leadership if mitigation requires cross-pool traffic.

I'll update within 30 minutes with a proposed mitigation.

—Vanessa
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: throughput-snapshot-20270904.csv

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: errors + latency on reserved pool (Aurora production)

Team — quick technical readout from infra: 

Observations:
1) QPS pattern: 07:38–07:50 saw a 3.8x traffic delta vs baseline on hot endpoints (session-scoring).
2) KV cache backlog: prefix cache hit rate dropped; write amplification caused KV queues to pile up. See attached kv-cache-backlog-snippet.txt showing queue depths hitting 18k per shard.
3) GPU pressure: GPUs on pool reported increased kernel eviction events; PGF scheduler started preempting larger batches leading to token jitter and retry storms.
4) Routing: a number of requests are pinned to a model variant that is not available in the nearest backup pool. That prevented graceful fallback.

Immediate mitigations executed (08:55–09:00):
- Flipped emergency routing to allow model-variant fallback across compatible pools (5–15% of traffic rerouted in waves).
- Purged stale KV prefixes for the affected namespace to recover cache capacity (~40% reduction in queue depth).
- Raised per-tenant concurrency cap to allow short burst while we stabilize.

Current state (09:02): p95 latency down to ~320ms, error rate to ~0.8%. However sustained tail remains above SLA for a subset of endpoints.

Recommended next steps requiring executive approvals:
A) Short-term burst authorization: allow cross-pool burst (estimated cost $18k/day) to avoid customer impact during their high-volume window.
B) Schedule a canary rollout for more tolerant routing rules so fallback can trigger earlier (ops + product approval).
C) Procurement path: propose a temporary reservation uplift for AU-7742 to increase baseline throughput while we rework kernel sizing for that model.

I attached the queue and stack snippets. Will follow up with a deeper RCA once logs and kernel metrics finish aggregating.

—David
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime

Attachments: kv-cache-backlog-snippet.txt

---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: CEO Leadership <ceo@redwood.ai>, CTO Ops <cto_ops@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec readout: AuroraBank reserved pool saturation — ask for burst authorization and credits

Folks — quick summary and asks (tl;dr below).

What happened: AuroraBank (AU-7742) encountered a rapid traffic spike at 07:38 PDT causing KV cache backlog and GPU kernel preemption across the reserved pool. That produced elevated p95 latency and a transient 5xx spike. Engineering mitigations reduced error rate from ~3.6% to ~0.8% but tail latency remains above the SLA for a fraction of routes used by their fraud model.

Customer impact: several scoring requests timed out at the gateway. Aurora is in a high-risk processing window this morning (batch reconciliation run) — potential revenue and user experience impact if we don't fully mitigate in the next 12 hours. They are actively monitoring.

What we did: emergency fallback routing, KV prefix purge, temporary concurrency cap increase. Partial relief achieved; backlog and GPU pressure trending down but not fully recovered.

Decision needed from leadership:
- Approve cross-pool burst authorization for Aurora (estimated incremental cost ~$18k/day) to avoid immediate business interruption. This requires temporary permission to allocate capacity from dedicated shared headroom.
- Approve a customer credit for the impacted window if we cannot deliver full SLA recovery within 24 hours (billing/CS direction).

If approved we will: execute a controlled cross-pool burst (ops playbook), open a post-incident RCA with Aurora within 48 hours, and schedule a technical remediation plan (kernel tuning + routing rule changes) with a target of 2 weeks to prevent recurrence.

Requested by EOD: authorization to open a burst allocation and go ahead on a customer goodwill credit iff we miss full SLA recovery.

Thanks — I will be available for a call.

—Vanessa
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
